about: Nightforge's own per-game profiles, tested on Macs. They take precedence over umu-protonfixes. Fields: graphics (dxmt|dxvk|wined3d|d3dmetal), arguments, dllOverrides, registry, windowsVersion, winetricks, metalFX (false = keep MetalFX off), frameLimit (automatic FPS limit), vulkanSamplers (samplers per shader stage reported to Vulkan games), preferWindows (true = Automatic keeps the Windows version although Steam has a 64-bit Mac one), saves (save folders for games without Steam Cloud rules, carried over when the game changes between its Windows and Mac version), antiCheat / antiCheatOnline ([] = runs on a Mac despite what AreWeAntiCheatYet says), notYet (a reason in plain English: the game doesn't start on a Mac yet and Nightforge is working on it; Nightforge says so before the download and offers GeForce Now when it has the game, loading and starting stay possible as a small button; the reason needs a German entry in Strings.swift), avx (false = start without Rosetta's AVX hint, for games that crash on it), fileEdits ([{path, find, replace, root, once}] in the game's own settings files before each start; path relative to its folder, or to root – a Windows root as in saves; once = a starting value, applied a single time), iniSettings ([{root, path, section, values}] set in the game's own .ini files before each start), retina (true = the game sees the full Retina resolution; Steam restarts when it changes), resolution ({root, path, fields: {width, height, fullscreen}} for a line of values separated by spaces, counted from 0, or {root, path, section, keys: {width, height, fullscreen}} for an .ini file; fullscreenOn: the values meaning full screen, 1 by default: where the game keeps its full-screen resolution, set to the screen it plays on before each start when that screen lacks it), environment (Wine's and CrossOver's own switches the game starts with, e.g. {"WINE_SIMULATE_WRITECOPY": "1"}: only the names GameEnvironment.allowed lists, values of letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'; anything else is dropped, and the profiles workflow refuses it), executable (the program to start instead of the store's, relative to the game folder: Epic's and GOG's games only, Steam picks its own; a game with a DirectX 12 program of its own beside the store's, like Control_DX12.exe, starts that one on D3DMetal without it), gog (the same game's GOG product IDs, which get this profile too), ignoreUpstream, note.

550.name: Left 4 Dead 2
550.note: Tested 2026-11-08 on M5, macOS 27.0, winecx 4.7.3, WineD3D: loading a map hung right after 'Redownloading all lightmaps' whenever sound was on. The game opens the microphone there, winecx asks macOS for it, and macOS refused because Nightforge's helper had no NSMicrophoneUsageDescription (tccd, all 12 runs with sound on 7./8.11.); -nosound skips that step and loaded. Not the cause: windows_speaker_config (4 is stereo, 2 mono), graphics backend (OpenGL or Vulkan), CSMT, mat_queue_mode, msync, Rosetta's AVX hint, CX_APPLEGPTK_LIBD3DSHARED_PATH. 2026-10-26: DXVK fails (MoltenVK rejects its buffers), -vulkan (Valve's DXVK) doesn't start.

50130.name: Mafia II (Classic)
50130.note: Tested 2026-10-31 on M5 with the GOG version (1816059595) on winecx 4.7.3. DXVK's Direct3D 9 gets no device on MoltenVK: it needs geometryShader and shaderCullDistance, which MoltenVK lacks (KosmicKrisp advertises both since Mesa 14f59d06). WineD3D plays, but in game two threads sit at ~95 % each (230-440 % CPU in all, the menu ~120 %) and the sound crackles and drops out. A 32-bit game on winecx's new WoW64: every OpenGL call is thunked, mapped buffers are copied, ARB_buffer_storage is off. APEX PhysX on or off, DirectSound instead of WASAPI (winxp) and low shadows, geometry and no AO made no difference (in game still 250-460 %, threads at 97/88/88/45 %). DXVK on a Vulkan driver with geometry shaders and placed memory mapping (KosmicKrisp) is the way out. Above ~100 FPS the game sticks in slow motion during police chases, so VSync stays on.

251570.name: 7 Days to Die
251570.note: Tested 2026-10-24 on M5: ~63 FPS with DXMT; with DXVK the game sees only 128 MB VRAM and drops to low textures and ~30 FPS. Steam's no-EAC launch option is picked automatically.

275850.name: No Man's Sky
275850.note: Tested 2026-10-25 on M5: the Windows version (Vulkan) starts on MoltenVK only with Nightforge's Vulkan layer, which drops wide lines and reports 32 samplers per stage (24 is still too few). Steam also sells a native Mac version.

1422450.name: Deadlock
1422450.note: Tested 2026-10-26 on M5: plays with DXVK at 60-120 FPS (the Vulkan layer's count). Steam may first ask about controller firmware; Nightforge shows that window.

1623730.name: Palworld
1623730.note: Tested 2026-10-26 on M5: steady 60 FPS (frame limit) with DXMT and -dx11. With DXVK only the HUD showed over a black world. Steam asks for the EULA once.

2357570.name: Overwatch
2357570.note: Tested 2026-11-07 on M5, macOS 27.0, winecx 4.7.3, the Steam version from Nightforge: reaches a match on DXMT at about 57 FPS, Direct in the Metal HUD, MetalFX spatial 1512x982 to 3024x1964. Needs CX_APPLEGPTK_LIBD3DSHARED_PATH (set for all winecx programs) and nvapi64 and nvngx off, as Recall does.

3132990.name: Black Myth: Wukong Benchmark Tool
3132990.note: Tested 2026-10-26 on M5 with D3DMetal 4.0b3 on winecx 4.7.3. DirectX 12 through D3DMetal: 70 FPS average, 56 in the slowest fifth (Niedrig, 1512x982, FSR), clean picture. DirectX 11 (-dx11) through DXMT: ~45 FPS with heavy texture noise. Crashes on an illegal instruction ~30 s in with ROSETTA_ADVERTISE_AVX=1, and at start with frame generation (InsertFrame), which it switches on by itself at its first start. Again 2026-11-01 on M5, macOS 27.0, with D3DMetal 3.0 imported from Apple (winecx 4.7.3): 68 FPS average, 83 at most, 55 in the slowest fifth (Niedrig, 1512x982, FSR), a few hitches at the start and one in the middle (shaders on the first run). Unreal's "Known issues with graphics driver" warning shows with 3.0 (it reports an AMD driver, 30.0.15.1233): Nightforge clears the AMD list in Hardware.ini.

3907790.name: OxyRail
3907790.note: Tested 2026-10-24 on M5: ~75 FPS with DXMT vs 45-50 with DXVK on Extreme.

3916150.name: The Last Caretaker Demo
3916150.note: Tested 2026-10-28 on M5 (Unreal 5.7.4). DirectX 11 fails on every layer: DXMT stays black while its graphics memory grows by ~400 MB/s, DXVK 3 on KosmicKrisp and D3DMetal crash. DirectX 12 through D3DMetal plays; with Rosetta's AVX hint it crashes after ~2 min (illegal instruction while precompiling shaders). Nanite and virtual shadow maps cost D3DMetal half the frame rate (30 -> 64 FPS without them, Engine.ini). With full Retina output (3024x1964), Low, FSR Performance and FSR frame generation: 50-55 FPS, sharp. Ray tracing and MegaLights stay off. The menu's background video stays black.

epic.45e7cf3c49054f2fb20b673d9b0ae69e.name: Sonic Mania
epic.45e7cf3c49054f2fb20b673d9b0ae69e.note: Seen 2026-11-01 on M5 with the Epic version on winecx 4.7.3: its first start writes Settings.ini (Sega/SonicMania in AppData/Local) with windowed=y at 848×480, so it played in a small window on the TV. windowed=n plays full screen at the desktop's resolution (no fsWidth/fsHeight in the file); exclusiveFS stays as the game sets it.

epic.calluna.name: Control
epic.calluna.note: Seen 2026-11-02 on M5, macOS 27.0.1, winecx 4.7.3 with the Epic version: Control.exe hands over to Control_DX11.exe, which ends right after creating its Direct3D 11.0 device (null page fault, no window), on DXMT and on DXVK alike. On Macs Control runs as Control_DX12.exe with D3DMetal (AppleGamingWiki, CodeWeavers); on D3DMetal Nightforge starts that program (it lies beside Control.exe). Not yet tested on D3DMetal.
